raw_text:
Below is a structured 12-week general fitness program tailored for a 58-year-old male, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise with heart rate targets below 70% of age-predicted max (roughly ≤115 bpm), no Valsalva, and no maximal lifts. It uses a full gym and gradually progresses in duration, intensity, and complexity while emphasizing cardiovascular safety, muscular endurance, mobility, and recovery.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Baseline: cleared for moderate-intensity exercise; ensure medical clearance remains current. Screen for new/worsening symptoms (chest pain, dizziness, undue shortness of breath, palpitations, or fatigue).
- Target intensity: preserve HR ≤115 bpm during most sessions. Use RPE (4–6/10) when possible if HR is challenging to monitor; discontinue if symptoms arise.
- Warm-up and cool-down: 8–10 minutes each, including light cardio and dynamic mobility; cooldown includesgentle stretch.
- Technique: no max lifts; focus on controlled tempo, emphasis on form, and breathing, especially avoiding Valsalva.
- Progression: gradual increases in volume first, then occasional intensity boosts via tempo, distance, or resistance, not by attempting heavier loads or high-intensity intervals initially.

Program structure
- Duration: 12 weeks, 3 training days per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu/Sat). Non-consecutive days to aid recovery.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Establish base endurance, technique, HR control, and movement quality.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build muscular endurance and confidence with higher volume and mild progression in resistance.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Further conditioning gains with refined technique, stability, and slightly higher effort within safe HR range; prepare for a maintenance plan.

Weekly structure (typical session)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min light cardio + dynamic mobility
- Resistance training: 30–40 minutes (adjusted by phase)
- Optional accessory / core: 10–15 minutes
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes, stretch and breathing

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Establish consistent routine, correct movement patterns, promote muscular endurance, learn HR pacing, and begin light resistance.

Session layout (3 days per week)
1) Cardio + mobility (5–10 min) + resistance
- Cardio: Treadmill walking or stationary bike
  - Week 1–2: 15–20 min continuous at light-moderate pace, HR ≤ 105–110, RPE 3–5
  - Week 3–4: 20–25 min, HR ≤ 110–115, RPE 4–5
- Mobility: 5 minutes dynamic hip, shoulder, thoracic spine.

2) Resistance training (major lifts with low to moderate loads)
- Superset block style to keep session efficient; focus on form.

Workout A (Upper)
- Seated cable chest press: 2 sets x 12–15 reps (light)
- Seated row (machine or cable): 2 x 12–15
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull-down: 2 x 12–15
- Dumbbell shoulder press (neutral grip, seated): 2 x 12–15
- Cable tricep pushdown (or overhead tricep extension): 2 x 12–15
- Core: plank regressions or dead bug: 2 x 20–30s

Workout B (Lower)
- Leg press or leg extension/clexion combo: 2 x 12–15 (each)
- Seated leg curl: 2 x 12–15
- Glute bridges (hip thrust on a mat): 2 x 12–15
- Calf raises: 2 x 15–20
- Core: side plank holds or pallof press: 2 x 12–15 per side

Work-to-rest: 60–90 seconds between sets; breath-control to avoid Valsalva.

Progression in Phase 1
- Weeks 1–2: 2 sets per exercise, 12–15 reps; emphasis on technique.
- Weeks 3–4: Increase to 2–3 sets per exercise if form remains solid; keep reps 12–15; slight resistance increase (2–5%) if comfortable and HR safe.

Phase 2: Build endurance and strength (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Increase training volume moderately; maintain HR targets; improve muscular endurance and movement quality; introduce light circuit elements to enhance cardio endurance.

Session structure (3 days)
Cardio portion
- Choose either:
  - Bike: 20–25 min steady-state at HR ≤ 110–115
  - Treadmill: brisk walk with incline intervals
    - 2 x 1-minute incline intervals at a mild incline (e.g., 3–5%), RPE 4–5, with 2 minutes easy pace between
- Option for intervals if well-tolerated: 1–2 rounds of 30–60s work/90s rest at HR not to exceed 120 briefly; otherwise keep steady.

Resistance training (full body split with increased volume)
Workout A (Push emphasis)
- Chest press machine or incline dumbbell press: 3 x 12–15
- Seated cable row (neutral grip): 3 x 12–15
- Overhead press (machine or light dumbbells, seated): 3 x 12–15
- Dumbbell lateral raises: 2 x 12–15
- Triceps pushdown: 3 x 12–15
- Core: dead bug or bird-dog: 3 x 12–15 per side

Workout B (Pull/Lower emphasizes)
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull-down: 3 x 12–15
- Seated leg press or goblet squat with light kettlebell/dumbbell: 3 x 12–15
- Leg extension: 3 x 12–15
- Leg curl: 3 x 12–15
- Glute bridges or hip thrusts: 3 x 12–15
- Core: pallof press or cable anti-rotation: 3 x 12–15 per side

Core and mobility
- Add 1 core circuit on one of the non-lifting days or post-training: 3 rounds of:
  - 30s dead bug
  - 12–15 slow mountain climbers
  - 15–20s farmer’s carry hold (light to moderate dumbbells if tolerated)

Progression in Phase 2
- Increase sets to 3 per exercise while keeping reps in 12–15 range.
- If HR permits, increase resistance modestly (roughly 5–10%) while maintaining technique and RPE.
- Include one optional circuit day per week with lighter weights and longer rest to promote endurance.

Phase 3: Conditioning and maintenance focus (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Solidify routine, build sustainable conditioning, refine movement mechanics, and prepare for long-term maintenance.

Session structure (3 days)
Cardio
- 25–35 minutes total with HR preferably in 105–118 bpm range depending on tolerance; alternate days:
  - Day A: Continuous cardio (bike or treadmill) at steady pace
  - Day B: Interval-style light: 1–2 minutes work at brisk pace, 2 minutes easy pace; repeat 6–8 cycles
  - Day C: Mixed: 15–20 minutes moderate pace + 5–10 minutes cooldown into mobility work

Resistance training (full body)
Workout A
- Chest press machine or incline dumbbell press: 3 x 12
- Seated row: 3 x 12
- Dumbbell shoulder press: 3 x 12
- Leg press: 3 x 12
- Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells (focus on hamstrings and back): 3 x 12
- Core: side plank 3 x 20–30s per side

Workout B
- Lat pulldown: 3 x 12
- Leg extension: 3 x 12
- Leg curl: 3 x 12
- Glute bridges or hip thrusts: 3 x 12
- Calf raises: 3 x 15
- Core: bicycle crunch or cable rotational chop: 3 x 12–15 per side

Tempo and technique
- Focus on controlled tempo: 2–0–2 (2 seconds down, 0 pause, 2 seconds up) for many exercises; adjust if necessary for safety.
- No maximal lifts; avoid locking out fully on any movement; exhale on exertion, inhale on release.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night.
- Nutrition: balanced intake focusing on heart-healthy patterns (lean protein, high-fiber carbs, healthy fats, vegetables). Maintain terminal caloric intake to support gradual weight stability or modest loss if clinically advised; ensure adequate hydration.
- Hydration: 2.0–3.0 L/day depending on activity and climate.
- Stress management: breathing routines, mindfulness or light activity on off days.

Exemplary week-by-week progression outline
- Weeks 1–2: Phase 1, sessions 3x/week; 2 sets x 12–15 reps per exercise; light resistance; cardio 15–25 min; emphasis on technique and HR management.
- Weeks 3–4: Phase 1 end with 2–3 sets x 12–15; cardio remains in HR range; introduce one additional mobility or core exercise per session; begin slightly longer cardio sessions (20–25 min).
- Weeks 5–6: Phase 2 begins; 3 sets x 12–15; add 1–2 resistance exercises per session; cardio 20–25 min with mild incline or intervals; include one circuit-style day per week if tolerated.
- Weeks 7–8: Phase 2 continuity; attempt small resistance increases (5–10%) where form allows; keep HR within target; maintain 3x/week.
- Weeks 9–10: Phase 3 begins; 3 sets x 12; add a brief interval or tempo progression within safe HR; total cardio duration 25–35 min when possible.
- Weeks 11–12: Phase 3 peak conditioning; maintain technique; introduce slightly longer conditioning blocks or one longer cardio session per week; ensure no signs of overexertion.

Monitoring and adjustment
- Heart rate: use HR monitoring whenever possible; if HR drifts above 115 bpm consistently, reduce resistance, reduce tempo, or substitute with longer rest.
- Symptoms: any chest discomfort, excessive fatigue, dizziness, or unusual shortness of breath requires immediate stop and medical check.
- Progress checks: at weeks 4, 8, and 12, assess comfort with exercises, movement quality, and overall energy. Consider re-evaluating with trainer to adjust plan if needed.

Optional progression cues for the trainer
- If client demonstrates excellent adherence and tolerance, you may add:
  - One extra core-focused day (20 minutes) on Week 6 onward
  - Light interval sessions in cardio with strict HR control (only if tolerated)
  - Slightly longer sessions, up to 60–70 minutes, provided HR remains within safe range and client is asymptomatic

Equipment considerations
- Primary: treadmill, stationary bike, rowing machine optional, chest press, row, lat pulldown, shoulder press, leg press, leg extension/curl, glute bridge/hip thrust, dumbbells, cables.
- Use machines to reduce stabilization demand and control movement patterns, especially early on.

Nutrition notes
- Emphasize heart-healthy pattern: lean proteins (fish, poultry, legumes), complex carbohydrates (whole grains, vegetables), healthy fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts), high fiber, and adequate hydration.
- Consider a modest caloric deficit only if weight loss is clinically appropriate; otherwise focus on fueling for training and recovery.
- Post-workout nutrition: a small meal or snack with protein and carbs within 2 hours after training to support recovery.

If you’d like, I can tailor weekly session-by-session detail for you (specific exercise choices, exact set/rep schemes per week, and targeted progressions) based on the client’s equipment availability and any comorbidities or preferences.
